message.content:
Explore the andesim repo at /home/nick/work/andesim. It is a hybrid RISC-V simulator driver: `./andesim` is a self-building C++ end-user driver (sources likely under driver/), which orchestrates an external QEMU (functional) and an external vsim (cycle-accurate) with a state handoff. Search breadth: very thorough.

GOAL: map everything the driver knows about the guest memory/address map, and how a new `--print-memmap` feature would plug into the CLI, so we can plan it.

Tasks:
1. CLI structure: where subcommands (run, list, ...) and options (--mode, --trigger, --engine, --mem-size, --pc-start/--pc-end, --verify, --ilm/--dlm/--hvm, --no-reset-baseline, etc.) are parsed. File:line. How `./andesim list engines` / `list models` is implemented. How engine `--describe` output is consumed (which fields exactly: ilm_size, dlm_size, hvm_size, others?). Is there a generic passthrough for extra vsim args?
2. Memory-map constants and derivations in the driver (file:line for each): RAM base (guest physical), --mem-size default, shared-mmap sizing (shm.cpp physical_mmap_bytes, the +1 page), v_scratch_gpa computation, the ELF-overlap rejection in cmd_run, ILM/DLM/HVM base defaults (expect 0xA0000000 / 0xA0200000 / 0x90000000) and how sizes flow from --describe to (a) QEMU -readconfig/-global geometry and (b) plugin args and (c) vsim --ilm/--dlm/--hvm args, l2c_base default (expect 0xE0500000), UART2 (0xf0300000) and SimControl/HTIF (0xe0080000) if the driver references them anywhere. Also how the QEMU command line is composed for hybrid (memory-backend-file etc.) and what -readconfig file it generates (quote the generation code).
3. grep the whole repo for `memmap`, `print-memmap`, `mtree`, `memory map` -- is there ANY existing support, doc mention, or passthrough related to printing a memory map (including in scripts/, docs/, tests/)?
4. Test conventions: list tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_*.sh, and read one or two to describe the harness convention (how they source setup, invoke the driver, assert stdout). This is the model for a new test.
5. docs/USER_GUIDE.md: give the section outline (numbered headings) and note where memory-map documentation would fit; also check README.md for the CLI synopsis.
6. Check ROADMAP.md / ROADMAP_ilm_dlm.md / ROADMAP_hvm.md for anything about memory map printing or address-map documentation plans.

Return a structured report with file:line for every fact, the exact list of --describe fields the driver parses, the exact constants (bases/sizes/defaults), CLI parse code shape (so we know how to add an option/subcommand), and test+doc conventions. Raw data, no fluff.

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- csr-transport-bringup: Bring up or audit the hybrid CSR transport for an Andes RISC-V core, given the AndeStar V5 SPA PDF spec and a built vsim engine. Covers the whole pipeline: mine the spec (CSR inventory, IM Requirement / existence conditions, access modes, reset values), classify transport dispositions, bind capability gates to the engine's config.inc, and validate with the reset-hart CSR probe (--probe), the manifest completeness check, --verify, and the e2e suite. Use this skill whenever the user mentions a new core, a new vsim engine, CSR transport / transportation, CSR capability or caps gating, IM Requirement, reset value table, which mode a CSR is supported in, probe-vs-caps mismatches, exec_progbuf cmderr faults, or --verify field mismatches on Andes/M-ext CSRs -- even if they do not say "bring-up" explicitly. Also use it for engine registration work: per-engine test files, CSR manifests, completeness ("nothing missed") checks, or adding a new config of an existing core.

1	// andesim command-line parsing.
2	//
3	// The grammar is deliberately tiny and stable across all subcommands:
4	//
5	//   andesim <cmd> [--mode M] [--engine E] [--trigger T] [positional...]
6	//                   [-- <verbatim engine args...>]
7	//
8	// The single most important rule is the `--` boundary: every token after the
9	// first `--` is captured verbatim into `passthrough` and is NOT interpreted by
10	// the framework. That is what lets `fast`/`cycle` forward an engine's whole
11	// native CLI (e.g. `-gdb tcp::1234 -S`) untouched, so users see one simulator.
12	#ifndef ANDESIM_CLI_HPP
13	#define ANDESIM_CLI_HPP
14	
15	#include <string>
16	#include <vector>
17	
18	namespace andes_sim {
19	
20	struct Cli {
21	  std::string subcommand;                 // e.g. "run", "list"; "" if none
22	  std::string model;                      // --mode fast|cycle|hybrid (field stays 'model': the concept, see list models)
23	  std::string engine;                     // --engine <id>
24	  std::string trigger;                    // --trigger marker|pc
25	  // Hybrid trigger args (empty => cmd_run applies the default). pc boundaries
26	  // are a symbol name or 0x address; the sizes stay strings here and are
27	  // parsed where they are used.
28	  std::string pc_start;                   // --pc-start (trigger pc)
29	  std::string pc_end;                     // --pc-end   (trigger pc)
30	  std::string mem_size;                   // --mem-size (guest memory; --mmap-size is a hidden alias)
31	  std::string kanata;                     // --kanata <file> (marker/pc ROI trace)
32	  std::string objdump;                    // --objdump <file> (kanata labels)
33	  std::vector<std::string> positional;    // non-flag framework args
34	  std::vector<std::string> passthrough;   // verbatim, everything after `--`
35	  bool help = false;                      // -h / --help (before `--`)
36	  bool dry_run = false;                   // --dry-run (build, run, test, ...)
37	  bool verify = false;                    // --verify (run --mode hybrid)
38	  bool gdb = false;                       // --gdb (fast: QEMU gdbstub; cycle: vsim JTAG + ICEman)
39	  std::string gdb_port;                   // --gdb-port (fast: default 1234; cycle: default 9104)
40	  bool has_passthrough = false;           // a `--` boundary was present
41	  std::string error;                      // non-empty => parse failed
42	};
43

45	// core; the argv overload adapts it for main().
46	Cli parse_cli(const std::vector<std::string>& args);
47	Cli parse_cli(int argc, char** argv);
48	
49	}  // namespace andes_sim
50	
51	#endif  // ANDESIM_CLI_HPP

1	// The phase-plan grammar driven by run_plan (F6), minus the dropped QEMU2
2	// step.
3	//
4	// A Plan is a list of Steps; each Step names an engine (by id, resolved against
5	// the F2 registry), the role to invoke it in (its `invoke` template key, e.g.
6	// "fast-leg" / "accurate-leg"), and a Trigger. run_plan spawns each leg in
7	// order, threads the drained hybrid_state_v1 file forward, and returns each
8	// leg's mcycle/minstret. Under the no-QEMU2-handback design every F6 step
9	// drains, so the hybrid cycle figure is the vsim-leg mcycle minus the qemu-leg
10	// mcycle.
11	#ifndef ANDESIM_PLAN_HPP
12	#define ANDESIM_PLAN_HPP
13	
14	#include <map>
15	#include <string>
16	#include <vector>
17	
18	#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
19	
20	namespace andes_sim {
21	
22	// The ROI delimiter for a step. `kind` is marker|pc; `params` carries
23	// kind-specific values (e.g. enter_pc, exit_pc) that F9 maps onto trigger
24	// args. F6 only exercises the default marker case (no params).
25	struct Trigger {
26	  std::string kind;
27	  std::map<std::string, std::string> params;
28	};
29	
30	// One leg of a plan: which engine, which invoke role, under which trigger.
31	// `extra_args` are verbatim tokens appended after the filled template and the
32	// trigger args -- the seam for user-forwarded per-leg flags (e.g. the vsim
33	// leg's --kanata), which are orthogonal to the trigger.
34	struct Step {
35	  std::string engine_id;  // "qemu" | "verilator:ax45mpv_premium"
36	  std::string role;       // invoke-template key: "fast-leg" | "accurate-leg"
37	  Trigger trigger;
38	  std::vector<std::string> extra_args{};  // default-init: keeps 3-field Step{} literals warning-free
39	};
40	
41	// A whole hybrid run. Every step loads `elf`; the shared mmap (`mem_size`
42	// bytes, at `mmap_path` or allocated by run_plan when empty) survives across
43	// every leg so memory threads through.
44	struct Plan {
45	  std::string elf;          // path to the ELF every leg launches
46	  long long mem_size = 0;   // shared-mmap size in bytes
47	  std::string mmap_path;    // "" => run_plan allocates one (F5) and owns it
48	  std::vector<Step> steps;
49	};
50	
51	// What one drain step measured (read back from its state file), plus the
52	// leg's captured stdout -- the guest program's own output (UART/semihosting)
53	// rides the engine's stdout and must flow through to the user. `st` is the
54	// full drained record (verify_oracle F4: run --verify diffs the vsim drain
55	// against the oracle leg's in-process, after run_plan removed the files).
56	struct PhaseResult {
57	  unsigned long long mcycle = 0;
58	  unsigned long long minstret = 0;
59	  std::string out;
60	  hybrid_state_v1 st{};
61	};
62	
63	// Aggregate outcome. `error` empty => every step matched its expected exit and
64	// drained a valid state file; `phases` then holds one entry per step in order.
65	struct PlanResult {
66	  std::string error;
67	  std::vector<PhaseResult> phases;
68	  // The concrete per-step argv run_plan built (after placeholder fill, qemu_cfg
69	  // staging, and state threading). Populated whether or not the steps spawn, so
70	  // a --dry-run can print the exact commands without executing them.
71	  std::vector<std::vector<std::string>> argvs;
72	  bool ok() const { return error.empty(); }
73	};
74	
75	}  // namespace andes_sim
76	
77	#endif  // ANDESIM_PLAN_HPP

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# `-readconfig` cfg -- its config.inc distilled to per-extension `[global]`
# properties -- and the andesim plan executor injects it into the QEMU fast leg
# so the functional engine runs the same ISA the cycle-accurate engine models.
#
# Two layers:
#   1. unit (fast, always runs): plan-test covers stage_qemu_cfg (probe ->
#      workdir/qemu.cfg, with the tolerant fallback) and the fast-leg-only
#      `-readconfig` injection. Pure; no engine.
#   2. engine contract (needs a built vsim engine; SKIPs otherwise):
#      sim_<cpu> --print-qemu-config exits 0 and emits a [global] block whose
#      driver is andes-<family>-riscv-cpu (the family the QEMU leg selects).
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# 1. unit: stage_qemu_cfg + the -readconfig injection contract
bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
PLANTEST="$ROOT/build/driver/andesim-plan-test"
[ -x "$PLANTEST" ] || fail "missing unit-test binary: $PLANTEST"
"$PLANTEST" >/dev/null || fail "plan unit tests (stage_qemu_cfg / -readconfig) failed"
ok "unit: stage_qemu_cfg + fast-leg -readconfig injection"

# 2. engine contract. Resolve a built vsim engine the way the driver does:
#    VSIM_BIN_DIR (env, then config.env) -- shared vsim_bin_dir from log.sh.
BINDIR=$(vsim_bin_dir)
SIM=$(ls "$BINDIR"/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -1)
if [ -z "$SIM" ] || [ ! -x "$SIM" ]; then
  ok "SKIP engine contract: no built vsim engine under $BINDIR (set VSIM_BIN_DIR)"
  exit 0
fi

out=$("$SIM" --print-qemu-config 2>&1); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "--print-qemu-config exit $rc: $out"
# family: sim_<family>_<variant> -> andes-<family>-riscv-cpu
base=$(basename "$SIM"); base=${base#sim_}; family=${base%%_*}
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q '\[global\]' || fail "no [global] block: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q "andes-${family}-riscv-cpu" \
  || fail "driver not andes-${family}-riscv-cpu: $out"
ok "engine contract: $(basename "$SIM") --print-qemu-config -> andes-${family}-riscv-cpu cfg"

# 3. end-to-end (no spawn): `run --mode hybrid --dry-run` prints both legs, and
#    the QEMU leg carries -readconfig <cfg> -- i.e. the probe -> stage -> inject
#    chain is wired. Needs the andesim binary + a fixture ELF; SKIPs otherwise.
BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
elf=$(ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf 2>/dev/null \
      || ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/*.elf 2>/dev/null | head -1)
if [ -x "$BIN" ] && [ -n "$elf" ]; then
  id="vsim:${base}"
  out=$(VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR" "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \
        --dry-run --engine "$id" "$elf" 2>/dev/null)
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'dry-run: 2 command' \
    || fail "dry-run did not print 2 commands: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q -- '-readconfig' \
    || fail "dry-run QEMU leg missing -readconfig: $out"
  ok "dry-run: hybrid command preview shows both legs + -readconfig"
else
  ok "SKIP dry-run check (need build/andesim + a tests/fixtures/*.elf)"
fi

fail() { echo "[FAIL] $*" >&2; exit 1; }
ok()   { echo "[ok] $*"; }

expect() {
  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2

  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}

cfg_val() { grep -oP "$1=\\K.*" "$_LIB_ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '"' | head -1; }

# it: VSIM_BIN_DIR env, then config.env ("" when neither is set).
vsim_bin_dir() {
  if [ -n "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"; return; fi
  cfg_val VSIM_BIN_DIR

2	//
3	// The caller asks for `size` bytes; we resolve a backing directory over a
4	// tier list (first fit wins, fit = size + 256 MiB free), allocate a sparse
5	// file with mkstemp+truncate, and print one status line that always names
6	// the chosen tier -- and, when we fell past /dev/shm, why. HSIM_MMAP_DIR
7	// pins a single tier (hard error if it does not fit; no fallback past it).
8	#ifndef ANDESIM_SHM_HPP
9	#define ANDESIM_SHM_HPP
10	
11	#include <functional>
12	#include <string>
13	#include <vector>
14	
15	namespace andes_sim {
16	
17	// Free-space headroom a tier must have beyond the requested size.
18	inline constexpr long long kMmapSafetyMargin = 256LL * 1024 * 1024;

20	// One backing-store candidate: the directory plus the label used in
21	// status/error messages ("/dev/shm", "~/.cache/andesim", "HSIM_MMAP_DIR=..").
22	struct MmapTier {
23	  std::string dir;
24	  std::string label;
25	};
26	
27	// resolve_mmap_dir result: the chosen dir ("" on failure) and, when a tier
28	// was skipped, a human note saying which and why ("" when tiers[0] fit).
29	struct MmapDirChoice {
30	  std::string dir;
31	  std::string note;
32	};

35	// returns the count and leaves `err` empty; on failure returns 0 and sets `err`
36	// to the argparse-style message. Fractional values truncate (1.5G -> whole
37	// bytes).
38	long long parse_size(const std::string& spec, std::string& err);
39	
40	// L26/F2: the physical shared mmap is one V-scratch page (HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES)
41	// larger than the program's --mem-size, so the V-register transport page sits
42	// just ABOVE the program's declared RAM. No program layout -- low stack, top-of-
43	// RAM stack, or a heap grown to the ceiling -- can reach a page past its own
44	// RAM, so the scratch can never be clobbered. The vsim side parks the scratch
45	// at the mmap's top page (v_scratch_gpa), which equals ram_base + program_bytes.
